To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the optimal level of public catastrophic coverage is zero if the public sector has a lower marginal cost of providing coverage than the private sector; (2) the optimal level is less than 100 percent if the public sector's marginal cost is equal to the private sector's marginal cost; and (3) the optimal level exceeds 100 percent if public sector coverage is cheaper than private coverage.
